description: We are astronAUci, a team from Rzeszow building a Lunar Landing Site Navigator: a fast, intuitive and highly precise tool that shows where the Sun and Earth sit above the real lunar horizon at any landing site and date, so mission planners, educators and the public can judge solar power and direct-to-Earth communication windows in seconds. We are young, neurodivergent and we don't think like everyone else. Determination, love for space and creative thinking are what bring us together.
summary:
This project focuses on selecting optimal landing sites on the Moon. We verify each location by simulating the landing maneuver. The analysis takes into account the Moon’s orientation and motion relative to Earth. Based on this, we determine the time slots during which a landing in a given region is feasible.
The result of this work is a set of recommended locations, selected based on the lander’s parameters. For each site, we determine the available landing sites and mission timeframes.
Our analyses are based on reliable scientific data sources: NASA JPL Horizons (ephemerides and orbital geometry), NASA Moon Trek, and LROC QuickMap (topographic data and imagery of the Moon’s surface)
The project provides widespread access to advanced technologies in an accessible way. It combines complex data with a user-friendly interface 
and paves the way for the future popularization of sending rovers to the Moon. What makes it stand out, is the accuracy in predicting the positions of celestial bodies in the solar system up to 28 days in advance and impeccably modeled, rescaled orbits.
details:
Technology Stack:

Programming Languages: JavaScript (site rendering), Rust (backend development), CSS (frontend), HTML (frontend)

Key Tools: VSC: Used for checking and correcting minor errors in code

AI Assistants: Claude and Antigravity: for coding and research

Primary Data Source: The NASA POWER Project API, which provided historical data on celestial objects.

How It Works:

Upon opening the site, you’ll see a 3d model of the Moon. Hover your mouse over a landing site and click to see why we chose that specific location. You’ll also see time frames when landing is recommended, as well as detailed statistics on when, where, and how to land.

In addition to this, you can explore historical landing sites-such as Apollo 11-as well as crash sites from earlier missions and failed attempts.

Benefits and Impact:

Accurate measurements; a simple, clear, and user-friendly interface; a realistic depiction of the Moon powered by the official NASA Scientific Visualization Studio

| CGI Moon Kit; precise trajectories of celestial bodies powered by JPL HORIZON SYSTEMS

Impact: We want to introduce more people to the challenges of lunar lander missions; in the long term, we hope this project will serve as a foundation and inspiration for future generations, in line with our motto: “Inveni appuli, vici”

Innovation and Creativity:

Our project is innovative, because we want to blur the lines between software designed for professionals and the lack of software designed for everyday people. This is a program where you’ll see that as your skills grow, you don’t have to switch to other programs and relearn the interface and functionality. Through a creative approach to a complex problem, we’ve managed to achieve a balance that will satisfy everyone, regardless of skill level.

Team Considerations:

Our guiding principles for the project are:

-Is it designed to be easy to use?

-Does it provide professional data?

-Can its use encourage exploration of topics related to lander landings?
